transcript: So where I come from, I'm also part of Women's Heritage. Um, when a storyteller is revealing you with a story, they come to the end, and they say, C R I K, C R a C K y m N. And then the audience responds, story end. So let's practice story ends. I promise to keep this last one short and sweet before my friend kills me. To leave quietly. Well, matriarch, leader, warrior, captain, friend to all, these are just a few words to describe Malcolm Barry. You have been a beacon of light, goodwill, strength, and fortitude, Mel. You show us all the best parts of ourselves, and you're not afraid to tell us when we aren't being our best, either. You have LED us through this entire year, through incidents, award shows, and even now, right up to the last minute, guiding us through a slightly challenging time with love and compassion. You have been there. Her dressing room door is always open. Unless the key is out. And then, well, on your head, to be it, if you try to enter. Ha ha ha ha! You are powerful. You are beautiful. You are truly a magical human being. And we are blessed to have got to share the special person that you are. You are a shining star, a true professional, and one of the best damn storytellers that has ever graced this earth. Oh, yes. I promise. You are our breath. You are our Heartbeats, you are our home, and the gift you give us is truly appreciated every single day. There is so much more I could say about you, but we've got to get you to an award ceremony. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you for all that you are and all that you do. We love you so very much, and I'm going to miss you terribly. We love you, too, Oke.
classificationReason: A tribute/farewell speech to Mel La Barrie (Hermes in Hadestown West End). References the production and its cast but is a personal tribute to the actor, not a review of the show.
